📋 Your Memo 01 Initial Solution (Read-Only Reference)

This is the algorithm whose time complexity you must now analyse. Do not edit it here -- your analysis goes in Action 2-1 below.
Initial traversal pseudocode (Memo 01 Amendment 2)
FUNCTION FIND_MIN_COST_ROUTE(graph: Graph, entry: Vertex, exits: Set[Vertex]) -> Record{route: Path, cost: Integer}
   exitA <- GET_EXIT(graph, 'Exit A')
   exitB <- GET_EXIT(graph, 'Exit B')
   wings = graph['wings']
   junctions = graph['junctions']
   keyElements <- LIST(supplies) + [exitA, exitB]
   dist <- empty Dictionary
   paths <- empty Dictionary
   FOREACH u IN [entry] + LIST(supplies) DO
      dist[u] <- empty Dictionary
      paths[u] <- empty Dictionary
      SHORTEST_PATHS_DICT_CONSTRUCTOR(graph, u, keyElements, dist, paths, wings, junctions)
   END FOR

   best <- STATE_SPACE_SEARCH(entry, LIST(supplies), 0, [], dist, exitA, exitB, INFINITY, null)
   bestOrder <- best.order
   bestCost <- best.cost

   fullPath <- [entry]
   current <- entry
   FOREACH node IN bestOrder DO
      segment <- paths[current][node]
      FOREACH i <- 1 TO LENGTH(segment) - 1 DO
          APPEND(segment[i], fullPath)
      END FOR
      current <- node
   END FOR

   RETURN {route: fullPath, cost: bestCost}
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION INTRA_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node: Node, wing: Graph) -> Set[Node]
  RETURN wing.NEIGHBOURS(node)
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION INTER_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node: Node, junctions: List[Pair[Node, Node]]) -> Set[Node]
  nbrs <- empty Set
  FOR EACH (n1, n2) IN junctions DO
    IF n1 = node THEN
      ADD(n2, nbrs))
    ELSE IF n2 = node THEN
      ADD(n1, nbrs)
    END IF
  END FOR
  RETURN nbrs
END FUNCTION

FUNCTION ALL_NEIGHBOURS(node: Node, wings: Dictionary, junctions: List[Pair[Node, Node]]) -> Set[Node])
  w <- GET_WING(node)
  wingGraph <- wings[w]
  RETURN INTRA_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node, wingGraph) UNION INTER_WING_NEIGHBOURS(node, junctions)
END FUNCTION

PROCEDURE SHORTEST_PATHS_DICT_CONSTRUCTOR(graph: Graph, start: Vertex, keyNodes: List[Vertex], dist: Dictionary, paths: Dictionary, wings: Dictionary, junctions: List[Pair[Node, Node]])
   keyNodeSet <- SET(keyNodes)
   visitedKeyNodes <- empty Set
   visited <- empty Set

   pq <- empty Priority Queue
   INSERT(pq, 0, [])
   WHILE NOT IS_EMPTY(pq) DO
      (cost, path) <- POP(pq)
      current <- LAST(path)
      IF current IN visited THEN
          CONTINUE
      END IF
      ADD(current, visited)
      IF current IN keyNodesSet THEN
          paths[start][current] <- path
          dist[start][current] <- cost
          ADD(current, visitedKeyNodes)
      END IF

      IF SIZE(visitedKeyNodes) = LENGTH(keyNodes) THEN
          RETURN
      END IF

      FOREACH neighbour IN ALL_NEIGHBOURS(current, wings, junctions) DO
          IF neighbour NOT IN visited THEN
              edgeWeight <- graph.GET_EDGE_WEIGHT(current, neighbour)
              newPath <- COPY(path)
              APPEND(neighbour, newPath)
              INSERT(pq, cost + edgeWeight, newPath)
          END IF
      END FOR
   END WHILE
END PROCEDURE

FUNCTION STATE_SPACE_SEARCH(current: Vertex, remaining: List[Vertex], currentCost: Integer, order: List[Vertex], dist: Dictionary, exitA: Vertex, exitB: Vertex, bestCost, Integer, bestOrder: List[Vertex]) -> Record{cost: Integer, order: List[Vertex}}

   costToExitA <- currentCost + GET(dist[current, exitA, INFINITY)
   costToExitB <- currentCost + GET(dist[current, exitB, INFINITY)
   IF currentCost > bestCost OR (costToExitA > bestCost AND costToExitB > bestCost) THEN
      RETURN {cost: bestCost, order: bestOrder}
   END IF

   IF LENGTH(remaining) = 0 THEN
      costA <- GET(dist[current], exitA, INFINITY)
      costB <- GET(dist[current], exitB, INFINITY)
      IF costA < costB THEN
          chosenExit <- exitA
          exitCost <- costA
      ELSE
          chosenExit <- exitB
          exitCost <- costB
      END IF

      finalCost <- currentCost + exitCost
      IF finalCost <- bestCost THEN
          newOrder <- COPY(order)
          APPEND(chosenExit, newOrder)
          RETURN {cost: finalCost, order: newOrder}
      ELSE
          RETURN {cost: bestCost, order: bestOrder}
      END IF
   END IF

   FOREACH supply IN remaining DO
      stepCost <- GET(dist[current], supply, INFINITY)
      IF stepCost != INFINITY THEN
          newRemaining <- COPY(remaining)
          REMOVE(supply, newRemaining)
          newOrder <- COPY(order)
          APPEND(supply, newOrder)
          result <- STATE_SPACE_SEARCH(supply, newRemaining, currentCost + stepCost, newOrder, dist, exitA, exit B, bestCost, bestOrder)
          IF result.cost < bestCost THEN
              bestCost <- result.cost
              bestOrder <- result.order
          END IF
      END IF
   END FOR
   RETURN {cost: bestCost, order: bestOrder}
END FUNCTION
Initial algorithm description (Memo 01 Amendment 2)
# weighted_fac is available — weighted_fac['wings'][w] is wing w's NetworkX graph
# Edge weight: weighted_fac['wings'][w][(c1,r1)][(c2,r2)]['weight']
# Junctions: weighted_fac['junctions']  (list of ((w1,c1,r1),(w2,c2,r2)) pairs, cost=1)
# Entry: weighted_fac['entry']   Exit A: weighted_fac['exit_a']   Exit B: weighted_fac['exit_b']
import heapq
def find_min_cost_route(wfac):
  """Return (route, total_cost) for the minimum-cost path from entry to any exit."""
  # TODO: implement your weighted traversal algorithm here
  wings     = wfac['wings']
  entry     = wfac['entry']
  exit_a    = wfac['exit_a']
  exit_b    = wfac['exit_b']
  supplies  = set(tuple(s) for s in wfac['supplies'])
  junctions = wfac['junctions']

  def all_neighbours(node):
    """Return all neighbours of a (wing_id, col, row) node.
    Includes intra-wing corridor neighbours AND inter-wing junctions."""
    w, c, r = node
    # Intra-wing neighbours
    nbrs = [(w, nc, nr) for nc, nr in wings[w].neighbors((c, r))]
    # Inter-wing junction neighbours
    for n1, n2 in junctions:
      if tuple(n1) == node:
        nbrs.append(tuple(n2))
      elif tuple(n2) == node:
        nbrs.append(tuple(n1))
    return nbrs

  # Prepares a single dictionary that contains cost for every existing junction node, accessible for bi-directional traversal
  junction_costs = wfac.get('junction_costs', {(tuple(n1), tuple(n2)): 1 for n1, n2 in junctions})
  junction_lookup = {}
  for (n1, n2), cost in junction_costs.items():
    junction_lookup[(tuple(n1), tuple(n2))] = cost
    junction_lookup[(tuple(n2), tuple(n1))] = cost

  dist = {}
  paths = {}

  # Below function takes a start point (either the entry, or 1 of the supply nodes) and runs Djikstra from that node
  def Shortest_Paths_Dict_Constructor(start, key_nodess):
    nonlocal dist, paths

    # Cost for edge movement in network calculator - accesses junction_lookup dictionary if edge movement between wings
    def get_weight(u,v):
      w, c, r = u
      ww, cc, rr = v
      if w == ww:
        return wfac['wings'][w][(c,r)][(cc,rr)]['weight']
      return junction_lookup[(u, v)]

    key_nodes_set = set(key_nodess)
    visited_key_nodes = set()
    visited = set()

    heap = [(0, [start])]

    while heap:
      cost, path = heapq.heappop(heap)
      current = path[-1]

      if current in visited:
        continue
      visited.add(current)

      # Save current path and cost required to get from start node to current important node (another supply or exit)
      if current in key_nodes_set:
        paths[start][current] = path
        dist[start][current] = cost
        visited_key_nodes.add(current)

      # Terminate Djikstra only after having traversed and visited all important nodes
      if len(visited_key_nodes) == len(key_nodess):
        return

      # Append current node neighbours to priority queue (via heapq python library)
      for neighbour in all_neighbours(current):
        if neighbour in visited:
          continue
        new_cost = cost + get_weight(current, neighbour)
        new_path = path + [neighbour]
        heapq.heappush(heap, (new_cost, new_path))

    return None

  # Start, exits and supplies are key nodes, but nodes needing to be visited don't include entry
  key_nodes = [entry] + list(supplies) + [exit_a, exit_b]
  key_elements = list(supplies) + [exit_a, exit_b]

  # Run Djikstra for every important node
  for u in [entry] + list(supplies):
    dist[u] = {}
    paths[u] = {}
    Shortest_Paths_Dict_Constructor(u, key_elements)

  best_cost = float("inf")
  best_order = None
  collected_final = []

  # Branch and bound state space search - worst case is Brute Force but due to pruning, much more efficient
  def State_Space_Search(current, remaining, current_cost, order, collected):
    nonlocal best_cost, best_order, collected_final, dist

    # Pruning Condition
    if current_cost > best_cost or (current_cost + dist[current][exit_a] > best_cost and current_cost + dist[current][exit_b] > best_cost):
      return

    # End recursion on current branch if all supplies are visited
    if len(remaining) == 0:
      cost_a = dist[current].get(exit_a, float("inf"))
      cost_b = dist[current].get(exit_b, float("inf"))

      # Choose exit to visit based on which costs less to traverse to 
      if cost_a < cost_b:
        chosen_exit = exit_a
        exit_cost = cost_a
      else:
        chosen_exit = exit_b
        exit_cost = cost_b

      final_cost = current_cost + exit_cost

      # Rewrite the saved route if current discovery is better than best so far
      if final_cost <= best_cost:
        best_cost = final_cost
        best_order = order[:] + [chosen_exit]
        collected_final = collected[:]
      return

    # Recurse algorithm for every supply remaining to be visited (branching out)
    for supply in remaining:
      step_cost = dist[current].get(supply, float("inf"))
      new_collected = collected + [supply]

      # Only recurse if supply has valid distance (can be traversed to)
      if step_cost != float("inf"):
        new_remaining = remaining[:]
        new_remaining.remove(supply)
        State_Space_Search(supply, new_remaining, current_cost + step_cost, order + [supply], new_collected)

  # Start recursion from entry, having all supplies needing to be visited
  State_Space_Search(entry, list(supplies), 0, [], [])

  # Rebuild path based on saved best-case path and cost
  # Uses prebuilt paths dictionary to append adjacent node paths (Entry to supply, supply to next ...)
  full_path = [entry]
  current = entry
  for node in best_order:
    segment = paths[current][node]
    full_path.extend(segment[1:])
    current = node
  return full_path, best_cost

route, cost = find_min_cost_route(weighted_fac)

🧭 [M2-0] Worked Exemplars -- Two Algorithms, Two Complexity Classes

Before analysing your own algorithm, work through the two exemplars below. They are run on a fixed demonstration facility (seed 20260000) -- not your facility -- so their operation counts are not the numbers you quote in Part 5 of your own analysis. Both exemplars solve a problem on the same facility. Exemplar A ignores the supply units and routes straight to the nearest exit. Exemplar B collects all five supply units first. They differ by a single design decision, and that decision changes the complexity class -- not just the running time.
Why two? The most common error in this analysis is to add the cost of a repeated search instead of multiplying by the number of repetitions. Reading A and B side by side makes the difference visible: B runs the same kind of search k + 1 times, so its k appears as a factor, not a term.

The two algorithms in VCAA pseudocode

Exemplar A -- Nearest Exit (supplies ignored) 
ExitOnlyBFS(graph: Graph, entry: Vertex, exits: Set) -> Path:
1  frontier ← Queue containing entry              O(1)
2  seen     ← Set containing entry                O(1)
3  While frontier is not empty Do                 loop runs at most V times
4      current ← frontier.dequeue()               O(1) (V times)
5      If current in exits Do                     O(1)
6          Return ReconstructPath(current)        O(V) (once)
7      Foreach neighbour of current Do            2E times in total
8          If neighbour not in seen Do            O(1)
9              seen.add(neighbour)                O(1)
10             frontier.enqueue(neighbour)        O(1)
11 Return empty                                   O(1)
Line 3 contributes V, line 7 contributes 2E across the whole run, and the two are added because the neighbour loop is bounded by the total number of corridors, not re-run from scratch per sector. Tight upper bound: O(V + E).
Exemplar B -- Greedy Nearest Supply (collects all k, then exits) 
GreedyCollect(graph: Graph, entry: Vertex, exits: Set, supplies: Set) -> Path:
1  current   ← entry                              O(1)
2  remaining ← copy of supplies                   O(k)
3  route     ← list containing entry              O(1)
4  While remaining is not empty Do                loop runs exactly k times
5      target ← DijkstraToNearest(current, remaining)   O((V + E) log V) (k times)
6      route.append(PathTo(target))               O(V)
7      remaining.remove(target)                   O(1)
8      current ← target                           O(1)
9  target ← DijkstraToNearest(current, exits)     O((V + E) log V) (once)
10 route.append(PathTo(target))                   O(V)
11 Return route                                   O(1)
Line 5 is a complete search that costs O((V + E) log V), and line 4 runs it k times. A loop that repeats a search multiplies; it does not add. With the final run to an exit that is k + 1 searches, so the tight upper bound is O(k(V + E) log V).
The trap. Writing "O(V + E) for the search, plus O(k) for the supply loop, so O(V + E + k)" is the single most common error in this task. Check every loop: is the work inside it a constant-time step, or a whole search?
A -- nearest exitB -- greedy collection
Supplies collected0 of 55 of 5
Searches performed16 (= k + 1)
Operations measured6302097
Tight upper boundO(V + E)O(k(V + E) log V)
Envelope for that boundV + 2E = 902(k+1)(V + 2E) = 5412
Inside its own envelope?yesyes

The bound is whatever your implementation produces -- it is not guaranteed to be O(V + E); the marks reward precision in identifying the complexity of each pseudocode element and combining these logically, not reciting a standard result.
Address all five parts: Part 1 -- Annotate the elements. State the time complexity of each major element of your pseudocode: the outer queue/stack loop, the inner neighbour loop, and each operation (enqueue/dequeue/push/pop, visited lookup, marking visited). Give each in terms of V, E, or O(1). Part 2 -- Handle abstraction and recursion. If your algorithm calls a sub-procedure (traverse_wing, expand, neighbours) or uses recursion, state that unit's complexity and how many times it is invoked, making clear you are not double-counting. Part 3 -- Combine to a tight upper bound for your algorithm as you implemented it. There is no single answer to copy. Part 4 -- Do the variable costs change the class? The Amendment A2 corridor costs are now on the map. Explain whether introducing variable edge weights changes your algorithm's time-complexity class. (For BFS/DFS reachability it does not -- weights are just data attached to edges. Finding the minimum-cost path, however, needs Dijkstra at O((V + E) log V) -- a real change.)
